identity.name: Beeswax (white and yellow)
identity.chemical_class: Natural wax mixture (long-chain esters, hydrocarbons, fatty acids/alcohols)

function.mechanism: Forms a hydrophobic surface film that provides shine and a protective coating; this mechanism is inferred from regulatory use definitions for glazing/surface finishing.

adi.basis: OpenEFSA confirms a published 2007 EFSA opinion (ON-615) for beeswax and a later re-evaluation workflow withdrawn in 2012; a numeric ADI could not be retrieved from accessible official EFSA opinion text in this VM due publisher access challenge.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA has a published opinion record for beeswax as food additive (EFSA-Q-2006-021, ON-615, published 2007-12-20); the later re-evaluation track (EFSA-Q-2011-00756) is marked application withdrawn.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (evaluation year 2005), with comment of no safety concern at predicted exposure below 650 mg/person/day.

concerns.summary: Recent human-food-facing concerns in the literature are mainly about contaminants that can accumulate in beeswax matrices (for example pesticide or trace-element residues in hive products), rather than strong evidence of intrinsic toxicity of purified food-grade beeswax.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA (2005) ADI not specified with no safety concern at predicted exposure below 650 mg/person/day.
FDA 21 CFR 184.1973 affirms beeswax as GRAS direct food substance with cGMP-based use limits by category.
No beeswax-specific IARC monograph classification was identified in the current IARC list dataset.

populations: high consumers of comb honey where residue burdens in wax may be elevated
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric JECFA ADI is set (ADI not specified). EFSA numeric ADI could not be retrieved from accessible official pages in this environment. Residue-related concerns are context-specific and distinct from intrinsic E901 hazard.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory status is favorable (FDA GRAS with defined limits; JECFA ADI not specified/no safety concern), and no IARC classification or major bans were found. Main uncertainty is limited direct modern toxicology evidence on purified E901 plus contamination-driven risk scenarios in some wax-containing hive products.
key_factors: 21 CFR 184.1973 provides explicit GRAS use conditions and maxima
JECFA 2005 ADI not specified with no safety concern at predicted exposure
OpenEFSA confirms 2007 published opinion record and withdrawn later re-evaluation workflow
Recent PubMed evidence highlights contaminant residue concerns in wax matrices rather than clear intrinsic E901 toxicity
No IARC classification identified for beeswax
